23: 
24: /// Incremental evaluation state for event-driven FSE execution.
25: ///
26: /// This struct enables selector-by-selector evaluation, supporting streaming
27: /// input sources (e.g., JSON tokenizer) and early termination as soon as all
28: /// required rules are resolved.
29: ///
30: /// # Example
31: ///
32: /// ```ignore
33: /// let plan = compile_rules(rules);
34: /// let mut state = RuntimeState::new(&plan);
35: ///
36: /// for selector in &plan.selectors {
37: ///     if state.should_terminate() {
38: ///         break;
39: ///     }
40: ///     let value = input.value_for(selector);
41: ///     state.apply(&plan, selector, &value);
42: /// }
43: ///
44: /// let result = state.finalize(&plan);
45: /// ```
46: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
47: pub struct RuntimeState {
48:     /// Per-rule decision states (parallel to plan.rules).
49:     decisions: Vec<RuleDecision>,
50:     /// Count of required rules still unresolved.
51:     pending_required: usize,
52:     /// Number of selectors scanned so far (the FSE proof metric).
53:     selectors_scanned: usize,
54: }
55: 
56: impl RuntimeState {
57:     /// Create a new runtime state for the given compiled plan.
58:     ///
59:     /// All rules start in the `Unresolved` state, and the pending required
60:     /// counter is initialized to the plan's required rule count.
61:     pub fn new(plan: &CompiledPlan) -> Self {
62:         Self {
63:             decisions: vec![RuleDecision::Unresolved; plan.rules.len()],
64:             pending_required: plan.required_count,
65:             selectors_scanned: 0,
66:         }
67:     }
68: 
69:     /// Apply a selector value, resolving all rules dependent on it.
70:     ///
71:     /// This method:
72:     /// 1. Increments the selector scan counter
73:     /// 2. Looks up all rules that reference this selector
74:     /// 3. Evaluates each unresolved rule's predicate against the value
75:     /// 4. Updates rule decisions and decrements the pending required counter
76:     ///
77:     /// This is the core FSE operation: one value extraction is broadcast to
78:     /// all rules sharing that selector.
79:     pub fn apply(&mut self, plan: &CompiledPlan, selector: &Selector, value: &Value) {
80:         self.selectors_scanned += 1;
81: 
82:         if let Some(rule_indexes) = plan.path_index.get(selector) {
83:             for &rule_idx in rule_indexes {
84:                 if self.decisions[rule_idx] != RuleDecision::Unresolved {
85:                     continue;
86:                 }
87:                 let rule = &plan.rules[rule_idx];
88:                 let ok = predicate_matches(value, &rule.predicate);
89:                 self.decisions[rule_idx] = if ok {
90:                     RuleDecision::True
91:                 } else {
92:                     RuleDecision::False
93:                 };
94:                 if rule.required {
95:                     self.pending_required = self.pending_required.saturating_sub(1);
96:                 }
97:             }
98:         }
99:     }
100: 
101:     /// Check if evaluation can terminate early.
102:     ///
103:     /// Returns `true` when all required rules have been resolved (either True
104:     /// or False), allowing the caller to stop scanning selectors.
105:     ///
106:     /// This is a key FSE optimization: once all required rules are decided,
107:     /// optional rules don't need to be evaluated.
108:     pub fn should_terminate(&self) -> bool {
109:         self.pending_required == 0
110:     }
111: 
112:     /// Finalize evaluation with fail-closed semantics and return the result.
113:     ///
114:     /// Any required rule still in the `Unresolved` state is forced to `False`.
115:     /// The final `allow` decision is `true` only if all required rules are `True`.
116:     ///
117:     /// This method consumes the state.
118:     pub fn finalize(mut self, plan: &CompiledPlan) -> RuntimeResult {
119:         // Fail closed: any unresolved required rule is forced false.
120:         for (idx, rule) in plan.rules.iter().enumerate() {
121:             if rule.required && self.decisions[idx] == RuleDecision::Unresolved {
122:                 self.decisions[idx] = RuleDecision::False;
123:             }
124:         }
125: 
126:         let allow = plan
127:             .rules
128:             .iter()
129:             .enumerate()
130:             .filter(|(_, r)| r.required)
131:             .all(|(i, _)| self.decisions[i] == RuleDecision::True);
132: 
133:         let outcomes = plan
134:             .rules
135:             .iter()
136:             .enumerate()
137:             .map(|(idx, rule)| RuleOutcome {
138:                 rule_id: rule.id.clone(),
139:                 decision: self.decisions[idx].clone(),
140:             })
141:             .collect();
142: 
143:         RuntimeResult {
144:             outcomes,
145:             selectors_scanned: self.selectors_scanned,
146:             allow,
147:         }
148:     }
149: }
150: 
151: /// Execute a compiled FSE plan against an input in a single pass.
152: ///
153: /// This is a convenience wrapper around `RuntimeState` for batch evaluation.
154: /// For streaming or incremental evaluation, use `RuntimeState` directly.
155: ///
156: /// For each unique selector in the plan:
157: /// 1. Extract the value once from the input
158: /// 2. Broadcast to all rules sharing that selector
159: /// 3. Resolve each rule's state
160: /// 4. Early-exit when all required rules are resolved
161: ///
162: /// After the loop, any still-unresolved required rules are forced to False
163: /// (fail-closed semantics).
164: pub fn execute<I: InputProvider>(plan: &CompiledPlan, input: &I) -> RuntimeResult {
165:     let mut state = RuntimeState::new(plan);
166: 
167:     for selector in &plan.selectors {
168:         if state.should_terminate() {
169:             break;
170:         }
171:         let value = input.value_for(selector);
172:         state.apply(plan, selector, &value);
173:     }
174: 
175:     state.finalize(plan)
176: }
177: 
178: fn predicate_matches(value: &Value, predicate: &Predicate) -> bool {
179:     match (value, predicate) {
180:         (Value::String(v), Predicate::EqString(expected)) => v == expected,
181:         (Value::Bool(v), Predicate::BoolIsTrue) => *v,
182:         (Value::U64(v), Predicate::MaxU64(limit)) => v <= limit,
183:         (Value::Strings(values), Predicate::ContainsString(required)) => {
184:             values.iter().any(|v| v == required)
185:         }
186:         (Value::U64(v), Predicate::MinU64(limit)) => v >= limit,
187:         (Value::Missing, Predicate::Exists) => false,
188:         (_, Predicate::Exists) => true,
189:         (Value::String(v), Predicate::InSet(set)) => set.contains(v),
190:         _ => false,
191:     }
192: }

1: use super::model::{Rule, Selector};
2: use std::collections::HashMap;
3: 
4: /// Pre-compiled execution plan with deduplicated selectors and path index.
5: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
6: pub struct CompiledPlan {
7:     /// All rules in insertion order.
8:     pub rules: Vec<Rule>,
9:     /// Unique selectors in insertion order (deduplicated).
10:     pub selectors: Vec<Selector>,
11:     /// Maps each selector to the indices of rules that reference it.
12:     pub path_index: HashMap<Selector, Vec<usize>>,
13:     /// Count of rules marked `required: true`.
14:     pub required_count: usize,
15: }
16: 
17: /// Compile a set of rules into a fused execution plan.
18: ///
19: /// This deduplicates selectors so that evaluation iterates over unique selectors
20: /// (not rules), achieving the O(unique_selectors) invariant.
21: pub fn compile_rules(rules: Vec<Rule>) -> CompiledPlan {
22:     let mut selectors: Vec<Selector> = Vec::new();
23:     let mut path_index: HashMap<Selector, Vec<usize>> = HashMap::new();
24:     let mut required_count = 0usize;
25: 
26:     for (i, rule) in rules.iter().enumerate() {
27:         if rule.required {
28:             required_count += 1;
29:         }
30:         if !selectors.contains(&rule.selector) {
31:             selectors.push(rule.selector.clone());
32:         }
33:         path_index.entry(rule.selector.clone()).or_default().push(i);
34:     }
35: 
36:     CompiledPlan {
37:         rules,
38:         selectors,
39:         path_index,
40:         required_count,
41:     }
42: }

1: //! Default FSE plan compilation for Gatewarden validation.
2: //!
3: //! This module provides `compile_default_plan()`, which builds a hardcoded
4: //! FSE plan covering:
5: //! - Signature verification (crypto.signature_verified)
6: //! - License state validity (response.state_valid)
7: //! - Required entitlements (entitlements.required_N)
8: 
9: use super::compiler::{compile_rules, CompiledPlan};
10: use super::model::{Predicate, Rule, Selector};
11: use crate::config::GatewardenConfig;
12: use crate::GatewardenError;
13: 
14: /// Compile the default FSE plan for Gatewarden license validation.
15: ///
16: /// This creates a set of required rules that all licenses must pass:
17: /// 1. **crypto.signature_verified** — Ed25519 signature must be present and valid
18: /// 2. **response.state_valid** — Keygen's `meta.valid` must be true
19: /// 3. **entitlements.required_N** — Each required entitlement from config must be present
20: ///
21: /// # Arguments
22: ///
23: /// * `config` - The Gatewarden configuration containing required entitlements
24: ///
25: /// # Returns
26: ///
27: /// A compiled FSE plan ready for execution, or an error if compilation fails.
28: ///
29: /// # Example
30: ///
31: /// ```ignore
32: /// let config = GatewardenConfig { required_entitlements: vec!["PREMIUM".into()], ..Default::default() };
33: /// let plan = compile_default_plan(&config)?;
34: /// // plan now has 3 rules: signature_verified, state_valid, entitlements.required_0
35: /// ```
36: pub fn compile_default_plan(config: &GatewardenConfig) -> Result<CompiledPlan, GatewardenError> {
37:     let mut rules = vec![
38:         Rule {
39:             id: "crypto.signature_verified".to_string(),
40:             selector: Selector::SignaturePresent,
41:             predicate: Predicate::BoolIsTrue,
42:             required: true,
43:         },
44:         Rule {
45:             id: "response.state_valid".to_string(),
46:             selector: Selector::StateValid,
47:             predicate: Predicate::BoolIsTrue,
48:             required: true,
49:         },
50:     ];
51: 
52:     // Add entitlement rules from config
53:     for (i, ent) in config.required_entitlements.iter().enumerate() {
54:         rules.push(Rule {
55:             id: format!("entitlements.required_{}", i),
56:             selector: Selector::Entitlements,
57:             predicate: Predicate::ContainsString(ent.clone()),
58:             required: true,
59:         });
60:     }
61: 
62:     // Merge caller-supplied custom rules (e.g. usage caps via `UsageRemaining`).
63:     for rule in &config.custom_rules {
64:         rules.push(rule.clone());
65:     }
66: 
67:     Ok(compile_rules(rules))
68: }

1: //! Gatewarden-specific FSE input provider.
2: //!
3: //! This module defines `GatewardenEvalInput`, which implements the `InputProvider`
4: //! trait using `LicenseState` extracted from Keygen API responses.
5: 
6: use super::model::{InputProvider, Selector, Value};
7: use crate::protocol::models::LicenseState;
8: 
9: /// FSE input provider built from validated Gatewarden license responses.
10: ///
11: /// This struct wraps `LicenseState` and provides selector values for
12: /// Gatewarden-specific policy evaluation.
13: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
14: pub struct GatewardenEvalInput {
15:     /// The normalized license state from Keygen.
16:     state: LicenseState,
17:     /// Whether the response signature was cryptographically verified.
18:     signature_verified: bool,
19:     /// Locally-metered consumption for this license (from the `meter` feature),
20:     /// used to compute the `UsageRemaining` selector. `None` when unknown.
21:     local_uses: Option<u64>,
22: }
23: 
24: impl GatewardenEvalInput {
25:     /// Construct a new input provider from a validated license response.
26:     ///
27:     /// # Arguments
28:     ///
29:     /// * `state` - The normalized license state extracted from Keygen response
30:     /// * `signature_verified` - Whether the Ed25519 signature was valid
31:     /// * `local_uses` - Locally-metered consumption count (`None` if unknown / feature off)
32:     ///
33:     /// # Example
34:     ///
35:     /// ```ignore
36:     /// let state = LicenseState::from_keygen_response(&response)?;
37:     /// let input = GatewardenEvalInput::from_validated_response(state, true, None);
38:     /// ```
39:     pub fn from_validated_response(
40:         state: LicenseState,
41:         signature_verified: bool,
42:         local_uses: Option<u64>,
43:     ) -> Self {
44:         Self {
45:             state,
46:             signature_verified,
47:             local_uses,
48:         }
49:     }
50: }
51: 
52: impl InputProvider for GatewardenEvalInput {
53:     /// Extract the value for a given selector from this input.
54:     ///
55:     /// Maps FSE selectors to fields in `LicenseState`:
56:     ///
57:     /// - `SignaturePresent` → `signature_verified` bool
58:     /// - `StateCode` → `state.code` (e.g., "VALID", "EXPIRED")
59:     /// - `StateValid` → `state.valid` bool
60:     /// - `Entitlements` → `state.entitlements` Vec<String>
61:     /// - `ExpiresAt` → presence check on `state.expires_at`
62:     /// - `UsageRemaining` → Missing (future feature)
63:     fn value_for(&self, selector: &Selector) -> Value {
64:         match selector {
65:             Selector::SignaturePresent => Value::Bool(self.signature_verified),
66:             Selector::StateCode => Value::String(self.state.code.clone()),
67:             Selector::StateValid => Value::Bool(self.state.valid),
68:             Selector::Entitlements => Value::Strings(self.state.entitlements.clone()),
69:             Selector::ExpiresAt => {
70:                 if self.state.expires_at.is_some() {
71:                     Value::Bool(true)
72:                 } else {
73:                     Value::Missing
74:                 }
75:             }
76:             Selector::UsageRemaining => {
77:                 // Remaining allowed uses = max_uses - (Keygen current_uses + local meter count).
78:                 // `local_uses` is supplied by the manager (0/none when the `meter` feature is
79:                 // off or unknown); when the cap is not yet known this stays `Missing`.
80:                 match (
81:                     self.state.max_uses,
82:                     self.state.current_uses,
83:                     self.local_uses,
84:                 ) {
85:                     (Some(max), Some(current), local) => {
86:                         let used = current + local.unwrap_or(0);
87:                         Value::U64(max.saturating_sub(used))
88:                     }
89:                     _ => Value::Missing,
90:                 }
91:             }
92:             // Other selectors not applicable to Gatewarden validation context
93:             _ => Value::Missing,
94:         }
95:     }
96: }

47: /// Single, documented HTTP status contract shared by all validation routes.
48: ///
49: /// - Upstream/security failures (signature, digest, freshness, cache tamper,
50: ///   transport) → `502 BAD_GATEWAY`: the failure is not the caller's fault.
51: /// - Configuration failures → `500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR`.
52: /// - License-logic failures (invalid/expired, missing entitlement, usage limit,
53: ///   cache expired) → `200 OK` with `valid: false` for the caller to inspect.
54: fn error_status(e: &GatewardenError) -> axum::http::StatusCode {
55:     match e {
56:         GatewardenError::SignatureInvalid
57:         | GatewardenError::SignatureMissing
58:         | GatewardenError::DigestMismatch
59:         | GatewardenError::ResponseTooOld { .. }
60:         | GatewardenError::ResponseFromFuture
61:         | GatewardenError::CacheTampered
62:         | GatewardenError::KeygenTransport(_) => axum::http::StatusCode::BAD_GATEWAY,
63:         GatewardenError::ConfigError(_) => axum::http::StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR,
64:         _ => axum::http::StatusCode::OK,
65:     }
66: }

68: /// Whether an error result was derived from the authenticated cache.

73:     matches!(
74:         e,

77: }

295: /// Axum middleware: reject requests that exceed the configured per-IP rate limit.
296: ///
297: /// The client IP is taken from the real TCP peer address (`ConnectInfo`), which
298: /// is NOT attacker-controllable. Client-supplied headers such as
299: /// `X-Forwarded-For` are deliberately ignored, because trusting them would let
300: /// any caller reset their own bucket by spoofing a fresh IP on every request.
301: pub async fn rate_limit_layer(
302:     State(state): State<Arc<AppState>>,
303:     req: Request<Body>,
304:     next: Next,
305: ) -> Result<Response, (StatusCode, Json<ErrorEnvelope>)> {
306:     let ip = extract_client_ip(&req);
307:     if !state.rate_limiter.check_and_consume(ip) {
308:         return Err((
309:             StatusCode::TOO_MANY_REQUESTS,

319: /// Determine the client IP from the TCP peer address (`ConnectInfo`).
320: ///
321: /// Falls back to loopback only if connection info is unavailable (e.g. in unit
322: /// tests). Deliberately does NOT read `X-Forwarded-For`/`X-Real-IP`: those are
323: /// caller-controlled and would make the rate limiter trivially bypassable.
324: fn extract_client_ip(req: &Request<Body>) -> IpAddr {
325:     req.extensions()
326:         .get::<ConnectInfo<SocketAddr>>()
327:         .map(|ci| ci.0.ip())
328:         .unwrap_or(IpAddr::V4(Ipv4Addr::LOCALHOST))
329: }

1: //! Bearer-token middleware and per-IP rate limiter for the bridge.
2: //!
3: //! When `bearer_token` is set in bridge.toml every request to `/v1/*` must
4: //! carry `X-Bridge-Token: <token>` with the exact configured value.
5: //! A constant-time comparison prevents timing side-channels.
6: 
7: use axum::{
8:     body::Body,
9:     extract::Request,
10:     http::{HeaderMap, StatusCode},
11:     middleware::Next,
12:     response::Response,
13:     Json,

24: // ─── Bearer token check ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
25: 
26: /// Axum middleware layer: reject requests missing or with wrong X-Bridge-Token.
27: /// `expected` is `None` when no token is configured (middleware is a no-op).
28: pub async fn require_bearer_token(
29:     headers: HeaderMap,
30:     expected: Option<String>,
31:     req: Request<Body>,
32:     next: Next,
33: ) -> Result<Response, (StatusCode, Json<ErrorEnvelope>)> {
34:     let Some(expected_val) = expected else {
35:         // No token configured — pass through.
36:         return Ok(next.run(req).await);
37:     };
38: 
39:     let provided = headers
40:         .get("x-bridge-token")
41:         .and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok())
42:         .unwrap_or("");
43: 
44:     if !constant_time_eq(provided.as_bytes(), expected_val.as_bytes()) {
45:         return Err((
46:             StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED,
47:             Json(ErrorEnvelope {
48:                 error: "Missing or invalid X-Bridge-Token header".to_string(),
49:                 code: "UNAUTHORIZED".to_string(),
50:             }),
51:         ));
52:     }
53: 
54:     Ok(next.run(req).await)
55: }
56: 
57: /// Constant-time byte-slice comparison — prevents timing oracle on the token.
58: fn constant_time_eq(a: &[u8], b: &[u8]) -> bool {
59:     if a.len() != b.len() {
60:         return false;
61:     }
62:     let mut diff = 0u8;
63:     for (x, y) in a.iter().zip(b.iter()) {
64:         diff |= x ^ y;
65:     }
66:     diff == 0
67: }

69: // ─── Token-bucket rate limiter ────────────────────────────────────────────────
70: 
71: /// Per-IP token bucket entry.
72: struct Bucket {
73:     tokens: f64,
74:     last_refill: Instant,
75: }
76: 
77: /// Shared in-process rate limiter keyed by client IP.
78: pub struct RateLimiter {
79:     buckets: Mutex<HashMap<IpAddr, Bucket>>,
80:     /// Maximum requests per second per IP.
81:     rps: f64,
82:     /// Maximum burst = rps * BURST_MULTIPLIER.
83:     capacity: f64,
84: }
85: 
86: const BURST_MULTIPLIER: f64 = 3.0;
87: 
88: impl RateLimiter {
89:     pub fn new(rps: u32) -> Self {
90:         let rps_f = rps as f64;
91:         Self {
92:             buckets: Mutex::new(HashMap::new()),
93:             rps: rps_f,
94:             capacity: rps_f * BURST_MULTIPLIER,
95:         }
96:     }
97: 
98:     /// Returns true if the request is within the rate limit, consuming one token.
99:     pub fn check_and_consume(&self, ip: IpAddr) -> bool {
100:         let now = Instant::now();
101:         let mut buckets = self.buckets.lock().expect("rate limiter lock poisoned");
102:         let bucket = buckets.entry(ip).or_insert_with(|| Bucket {
103:             tokens: self.capacity,
104:             last_refill: now,
105:         });
106: 
107:         // Refill tokens based on elapsed time.
108:         let elapsed = now.duration_since(bucket.last_refill).as_secs_f64();
109:         bucket.tokens = (bucket.tokens + elapsed * self.rps).min(self.capacity);
110:         bucket.last_refill = now;
111: 
112:         if bucket.tokens >= 1.0 {
113:             bucket.tokens -= 1.0;
114:             true
115:         } else {
116:             false
117:         }
118:     }
119: 
120:     /// Prune entries that haven't been seen in over 60 seconds (background hygiene).
121:     pub fn prune(&self) {
122:         let threshold = Duration::from_secs(60);
123:         let now = Instant::now();
124:         let mut buckets = self.buckets.lock().expect("rate limiter lock poisoned");
125:         buckets.retain(|_, b| now.duration_since(b.last_refill) < threshold);
126:     }
127: }

# Skill: export-last-session

# Export Last Session

Run the profile-wide export script. It finds the OpenCode session **for the current
working directory's project** (it looks up the project via `opencode db` and only
considers sessions whose `project_id` maps to the current directory or one of its
parents), exports it via `opencode export`, and writes a **standardized markdown
transcript** into the **current repository root** (it walks up from the current
directory to the nearest `.git`/`.hg`, falling back to the current directory). The file
is named `opencode-session-<slug>.md`, so re-runs never clobber across repos or
sessions.

**Default behavior: export the *previous* session, not the current one.** The newest
session in the current project is, by definition, the session you are running the
export *from*. The whole point of this skill is to hand the *prior* session's context
into a fresh chat, so the script skips the current (newest) session and exports the one
before it. Pass `-Current` to the script if you ever want to export the newest session
instead.

**Export a specific session by label or ID.** Pass `-Session <id-or-label>` to export
a particular session regardless of recency. The argument matches the session **ID**
(exact) or the **title/label** (case-insensitive substring). This overrides both the
default previous-session behavior and `-Current`. Use this whenever the user references
a session by name (e.g. "export the codebase research session") — just pass a unique
substring of that label. Example:

```bash
pwsh "$HOME/.opencode/export-last-session.ps1" -Session "codebase research"
```

## CRITICAL: picking the RIGHT session (the "wrong one" trap)

When the user says "use your export skill" to *recover the last real work session*,
never blindly take the script's default (newest-minus-one). Many past sessions are
**titled** "Export previous session to JSON" / "Export last session" but actually
*contain real work* — they were sessions where the user was figuring out how to export.
A title starting with "export" does NOT mean it is a throwaway meta-session.

**The robust procedure (memorize this — do not re-derive it each time):**

1. Get the session list as JSON. **Do NOT use `opencode session list` — it hangs
   indefinitely** (it waits on a daemon that is not responding). Read the DB directly
   instead, which is instant and returns the same fields (use the `id`, not the title):
   ```bash
   opencode db --format json "SELECT id, title, project_id, time_updated FROM session ORDER BY time_updated DESC"
   ```
2. Scan the list and pick the **actual last WORK session**, not an export-named wrapper.
   Use the session **ID** (e.g. `ses_0749ad9e0ffeyEi0YSirlw6XjZ`), not the title, to be
   unambiguous.
3. Pass that ID explicitly to the skill:
   ```bash
   pwsh "$HOME/.opencode/export-last-session.ps1" -Session ses_0749ad9e0ffeyEi0YSirlw6XjZ
   ```
   (`-Session` accepts an exact ID or a title substring; prefer the ID.)

If you ever grab the wrong one, the cause is almost always "trusted the title / took the
default instead of reading `opencode session list` and passing `-Session <id>`." Fix the
call, not the user's request.

## Renaming the CURRENT session (keep the list clean)

The session list fills up with meaningless "export last session" / "New session" titles.
After you have exported, **read**, and **understood** the target session, rename the
session you are *currently running from* to something meaningful using `-Rename <title>`:

```bash
pwsh "$HOME/.opencode/export-last-session.ps1" -Session <id> -Rename "GROUP BY mismatch fuzzer fix"
```

`-Rename` updates the current session's title in the opencode DB (the newest session for
this project). This is the LAST step of the export flow — only do it once you know what
the work was actually about, so the new title reflects the real subject.

**Full fidelity — no truncation, plus a working-tree snapshot.** By default the script
captures the *entire* transcript: tool inputs/outputs are **not** truncated (the
`-MaxString` cap defaults to `0` = unlimited, so the markdown can be large — that's
intentional and fine). Additionally, the export appends a **`## Working Tree State`**
section containing `git status --short`, the full `git diff` of tracked modifications,
and the complete contents of any new (untracked) source files. This makes the document
self-sufficient: a fresh session can read it and pick up *exactly* where the exported
session dropped — including uncommitted refactors — without juggling the live repo or
parsing JSON with Python. Pass `-NoWorkingTree` to skip the snapshot, or `-MaxString
<N>` to cap each string at `N` chars.

> Note: the working-tree snapshot reflects the *current* repository at export time. It
> does NOT replace committing your work — always commit before the session's context
> could be lost. The snapshot is a resume aid, not a version-control substitute.

Crucially, the export is **scoped to the current directory**, so a session from a
different repo/directory that merely happens to have been updated more recently will
never be picked up. The metadata block records the project directory for verification.

## How to run

Run this from the repository where you want the report (normally the session's
project directory — that is already the working directory in an OpenCode session):

```bash
pwsh "$HOME/.opencode/export-last-session.ps1"
```

The script prints the absolute path of the written file.

## Immediately read the exported session

This is **mandatory and part of the same action** — do not treat it as a separate
follow-up. The instant the file is written, read it in full (use the Read tool on
the path the script printed). Absorb the entire transcript — what was attempted,
what changed, what was decided, what failed, and what the next steps are — so that
you fully understand the prior context *before* doing anything else. Only after you
have read and understood the session should you report the file path back to the
user verbatim and proceed with whatever new work was requested.

The goal: when the user says "use your export skill" (or any trigger above), you go

## Notes
- The script lives at `~/.opencode/export-last-session.ps1` (global, profile-agnostic).
- Output is dropped **locally in the repo**, never into `~/.opencode`.
- **Full fidelity, no script-level truncation.** Tool inputs/outputs are written

- **Caveat — Read-tool display truncation.** When an agent *reads* the exported markdown

- **Batch export.** Pass `-Last <N>` to export the newest N sessions at once, each to its

  newest file to avoid duplication). E.g. `-Last 5` hands a fresh session the full recent
  trail. `-Last` overrides the default single-session selection.
- Override the output location if needed:
  `pwsh "$HOME/.opencode/export-last-session.ps1" -OutputDir <dir>`

36: function Format-Val {
37:     param($v)
38:     if ($null -eq $v) { return '' }
39:     if ($v -is [string]) {
40:         # MaxString <= 0 means "no limit" — we want the full transcript so a
41:         # resumed session has everything it needs, length be damned.
42:         if ($MaxString -gt 0 -and $v.Length -gt $MaxString) {
43:             return $v.Substring(0, $MaxString) + "`n... [truncated, $($v.Length) chars total]"
44:         }
45:         return $v
46:     }
47:     if ($v -is [System.Collections.IDictionary] -or $v.PSObject) {
48:         try { return ($v | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 6) } catch { return "$v" }
49:     }
50:     return "$v"
51: }

53: function Fmt-Time {
54:     param($ms)
55:     if (-not $ms) { return 'n/a' }
56:     try { return ([datetimeoffset]::FromUnixTimeMilliseconds($ms).ToLocalTime().ToString('yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss')) } catch { return "$ms" }
57: }

59: function Get-RepoRoot {
60:     param([string]$start)
61:     $cur = $start
62:     while ($cur) {
63:         if (Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $cur '.git')) { return $cur }
64:         if (Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $cur '.hg')) { return $cur }
65:         $parent = Split-Path $cur -Parent
66:         if ($parent -eq $cur) { break }
67:         $cur = $parent
68:     }
69:     return $start
70: }

72: function Get-NormDir {
73:     param([string]$d)
74:     if (-not $d) { return '' }
75:     return $d.Replace('\', '/').ToLowerInvariant().TrimEnd('/')
76: }

78: # Returns the subset of sessions that belong to the current working directory.
79: # A session "owns" the cwd when its recorded `session.directory` equals the cwd
80: # or is a parent of it. We match on session.directory -- the authoritative,
81: # per-session cwd that the engine writes on every session -- rather than the
82: # `project_directory` cache. That cache is frequently INCOMPLETE: a workspace
83: # that was never registered there (or whose registration was dropped) has no
84: # row, so a project_directory-based scope silently returns nothing and the
85: # script falls through to ALL sessions, exporting a foreign repo's session.
86: # Matching on session.directory makes scoping robust regardless of cache state.
87: function Get-CurrentSessions {
88:     param($all)
89:     $normCwd = Get-NormDir (Get-Location).Path
90:     return @($all) | Where-Object {
91:         $d = Get-NormDir $_.directory
92:         if (-not $d) { return $false }
93:         $normCwd -eq $d -or $normCwd.StartsWith($d + '/')
94:     }
95: }
96: 
97: # NOTE: `opencode session list` hangs indefinitely (waits on a daemon that is not
98: # responding), so we read the session rows directly from the SQLite DB via
99: # `opencode db --format json`, which is instant and reliable.
100: $SessSQL = "SELECT id, project_id, slug, title, agent, model, cost, " +
101:     "directory, " +
102:     "tokens_input, tokens_output, tokens_reasoning, tokens_cache_read, " +
103:     "time_created, time_updated FROM session"
104: $sessRows = opencode db --format json $SessSQL 2>$null | ConvertFrom-Json
105: $sessions = @($sessRows) | ForEach-Object {
106:     [PSCustomObject]@{
107:         id               = $_.id
108:         projectID        = $_.project_id
109:         title            = $_.title
110:         slug             = $_.slug
111:         directory        = $_.directory
112:         agent            = $_.agent
113:         updated          = $_.time_updated
114:         created          = $_.time_created
115:         modelRaw         = $_.model
116:         cost             = $_.cost
117:         tokens_input     = $_.tokens_input
118:         tokens_output    = $_.tokens_output
119:         tokens_reasoning = $_.tokens_reasoning
120:         tokens_cache_read = $_.tokens_cache_read
121:     }
122: }
123: if (-not $sessions -or @($sessions).Count -eq 0) {
124:     throw "No sessions found."
125: }
126: 
127: # Scope to the current directory's sessions so we never export a
128: # session from a different repo/directory just because it was updated more recently.
129: # Match on session.directory (authoritative per-session cwd), not the
130: # project_directory cache, which can be missing the current workspace.
131: $scoped = Get-CurrentSessions $sessions
132: if ($scoped.Count -gt 0) {
133:     $sessions = $scoped
134: } else {
135:     throw "No sessions found for the current directory ($(Get-Location)). The session DB has no session recorded under this path."
136: }
137: 
138: if (-not $sessions -or @($sessions).Count -eq 0) {
139:     throw "No sessions found for the current directory ($(Get-Location))."
140: }
141: 
142: # Resolve which session to export. Priority:
143: #   1. -Session <id-or-label>  (explicit; overrides everything else)
144: #   2. -Current                 (newest session = the one we're running from)
145: #   3. default                  (the PREVIOUS session: newest minus the current one)
146: if ($Session) {
147:     $norm = $Session.Trim().ToLowerInvariant()
148:     $target = @($sessions) | Where-Object {
149:         $_.id -eq $Session -or
150:         ($_.title -and $_.title.ToLowerInvariant().Contains($norm)) -or
151:         ($_.id -and $_.id.ToLowerInvariant().Contains($norm))
152:     } | Sort-Object updated -Descending | Select-Object -First 1
153:     if (-not $target) {
154:         throw "No session matching '$Session' found for the current directory ($(Get-Location))."
155:     }
156: } else {
157:     $sorted = @($sessions) | Sort-Object updated -Descending
158:     if ($Current) {
159:         $target = $sorted | Select-Object -First 1
160:     } else {
161:         $target = $sorted | Select-Object -Skip 1 -First 1
162:         if (-not $target) {
163:             # Only one session exists for this project; nothing to hand off, so fall
164:             # back to exporting the (current) session rather than failing.
165:             $target = $sorted | Select-Object -First 1
166:         }
167:     }
168: }
169: # Build the list of sessions to export. -Last N takes the newest N; otherwise a
170: # single session was resolved above via -Session / -Current / default.
171: if ($Last -gt 0) {
172:     $targets = @($sessions) | Sort-Object updated -Descending | Select-Object -First $Last
173: } else {
174:     $targets = @($target)
175: }

177: # Reconstruct the export object directly from the SQLite DB. `opencode export`
178: # hangs (waits on a daemon), but everything it would return is stored in the
179: # `session` / `message` / `part` tables. The `part.data` JSON already carries the
180: # exact shape the markdown builder expects (type / text / tool / state.input /
181: # state.output), so we just parse and forward it.
182: function Get-SessionExport {
183:     param([string]$id)
184:     $sessRows = opencode db --format json "SELECT id, project_id, slug, title, agent, model, cost, tokens_input, tokens_output, tokens_reasoning, tokens_cache_read, time_created, time_updated FROM session WHERE id = '$id'" 2>$null | ConvertFrom-Json
185:     if (-not $sessRows -or @($sessRows).Count -eq 0) { return $null }
186:     $s = @($sessRows)[0]
187:     $m = $null
188:     try { $m = ConvertFrom-Json $s.model } catch { $m = @{ id = '?'; providerID = '?' } }
189:     $info = [PSCustomObject]@{
190:         id        = $s.id
191:         title     = $s.title
192:         agent     = $s.agent
193:         projectID = $s.project_id
194:         slug      = $s.slug
195:         model     = [PSCustomObject]@{ id = $m.id; providerID = $m.providerID }
196:         cost      = $s.cost
197:         time      = [PSCustomObject]@{ created = $s.time_created; updated = $s.time_updated }
198:         tokens    = [PSCustomObject]@{
199:             input     = $s.tokens_input
200:             output    = $s.tokens_output
201:             reasoning = $s.tokens_reasoning
202:             cache     = [PSCustomObject]@{ read = $s.tokens_cache_read }
203:         }
204:         summary   = ''
205:     }
206:     $msgs = @(opencode db --format json "SELECT id, data FROM message WHERE session_id = '$id' ORDER BY time_created ASC" 2>$null | ConvertFrom-Json)
207:     $parts = @(opencode db --format json "SELECT message_id, data FROM part WHERE session_id = '$id' ORDER BY time_created ASC" 2>$null | ConvertFrom-Json)
208:     $messages = @()
209:     foreach ($msg in $msgs) {
210:         $md = $null
211:         try { $md = ConvertFrom-Json $msg.data } catch { $md = @{} }
212:         $role = if ($md.role) { $md.role } else { 'user' }
213:         $mparts = @($parts) | Where-Object { $_.message_id -eq $msg.id } | ForEach-Object {
214:             $pd = $null
215:             try { $pd = ConvertFrom-Json $_.data } catch { $pd = @{} }
216:             $pd
217:         }
218:         $messages += [PSCustomObject]@{ info = [PSCustomObject]@{ role = $role }; parts = $mparts }
219:     }
220:     return [PSCustomObject]@{ info = $info; messages = $messages }
221: }

+//! Bearer-token middleware and per-IP rate limiter for the bridge.
+//!
+//! When `bearer_token` is set in bridge.toml every request to `/v1/*` must
+//! carry `X-Bridge-Token: <token>` with the exact configured value.
+//! A constant-time comparison prevents timing side-channels.
+
+use axum::{
+    body::Body,
+    extract::Request,
+    http::{HeaderMap, StatusCode},
+    middleware::Next,
+    response::Response,
+    Json,
+};
+use std::{
+    collections::HashMap,
+    net::IpAddr,
+    sync::Mutex,
+    time::{Duration, Instant},
+};
+
+use crate::routes::ErrorEnvelope;
+
+// ─── Bearer token check ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+/// Axum middleware layer: reject requests missing or with wrong X-Bridge-Token.
+/// `expected` is `None` when no token is configured (middleware is a no-op).
+pub async fn require_bearer_token(
+    headers: HeaderMap,
+    expected: Option<String>,
+    req: Request<Body>,
+    next: Next,
+) -> Result<Response, (StatusCode, Json<ErrorEnvelope>)> {
+    let Some(expected_val) = expected else {
+        // No token configured — pass through.
+        return Ok(next.run(req).await);
+    };
+
+    let provided = headers
+        .get("x-bridge-token")
+        .and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok())
+        .unwrap_or("");
+
+    if !constant_time_eq(provided.as_bytes(), expected_val.as_bytes()) {
+        return Err((
+            StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED,
+            Json(ErrorEnvelope {
+                error: "Missing or invalid X-Bridge-Token header".to_string(),
+                code: "UNAUTHORIZED".to_string(),
+            }),
+        ));
+    }
+
+    Ok(next.run(req).await)
+}
+
+/// Constant-time byte-slice comparison — prevents timing oracle on the token.
+fn constant_time_eq(a: &[u8], b: &[u8]) -> bool {
+    if a.len() != b.len() {
+        return false;
+    }
+    let mut diff = 0u8;
+    for (x, y) in a.iter().zip(b.iter()) {
+        diff |= x ^ y;
+    }
+    diff == 0
+}
+
+// ─── Token-bucket rate limiter ────────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+/// Per-IP token bucket entry.
+struct Bucket {
+    tokens: f64,
+    last_refill: Instant,
+}
+
+/// Shared in-process rate limiter keyed by client IP.
+pub struct RateLimiter {
+    buckets: Mutex<HashMap<IpAddr, Bucket>>,
+    /// Maximum requests per second per IP.
+    rps: f64,
+    /// Maximum burst = rps * BURST_MULTIPLIER.
+    capacity: f64,
+}
+
+const BURST_MULTIPLIER: f64 = 3.0;
+
+impl RateLimiter {
+    pub fn new(rps: u32) -> Self {
+        let rps_f = rps as f64;
+        Self {
+            buckets: Mutex::new(HashMap::new()),
+            rps: rps_f,
+            capacity: rps_f * BURST_MULTIPLIER,
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// Returns true if the request is within the rate limit, consuming one token.
+    pub fn check_and_consume(&self, ip: IpAddr) -> bool {
+        let now = Instant::now();
+        let mut buckets = self.buckets.lock().expect("rate limiter lock poisoned");
+        let bucket = buckets.entry(ip).or_insert_with(|| Bucket {
+            tokens: self.capacity,
+            last_refill: now,
+        });
+
+        // Refill tokens based on elapsed time.
+        let elapsed = now.duration_since(bucket.last_refill).as_secs_f64();
+        bucket.tokens = (bucket.tokens + elapsed * self.rps).min(self.capacity);
+        bucket.last_refill = now;
+
+        if bucket.tokens >= 1.0 {
+            bucket.tokens -= 1.0;
+            true
+        } else {
+            false
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// Prune entries that haven't been seen in over 60 seconds (background hygiene).
+    pub fn prune(&self) {
+        let threshold = Duration::from_secs(60);
+        let now = Instant::now();
+        let mut buckets = self.buckets.lock().expect("rate limiter lock poisoned");
+        buckets.retain(|_, b| now.duration_since(b.last_refill) < threshold);
+    }
+}
+
+#[cfg(test)]
+mod tests {
+    use super::*;
+    use std::net::{IpAddr, Ipv4Addr};
+
+    #[test]
+    fn constant_time_eq_correct() {
+        assert!(constant_time_eq(b"hello", b"hello"));
+        assert!(!constant_time_eq(b"hello", b"world"));
+        assert!(!constant_time_eq(b"short", b"longer_string"));
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn rate_limiter_allows_within_limit() {
+        let limiter = RateLimiter::new(10);
+        let ip: IpAddr = IpAddr::V4(Ipv4Addr::new(127, 0, 0, 1));
+        // First 30 requests (burst capacity = 10 * 3.0) should all pass.
+        for _ in 0..30 {
+            assert!(limiter.check_and_consume(ip));
+        }
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn rate_limiter_rejects_over_burst() {
+        let limiter = RateLimiter::new(10); // burst = 30
+        let ip: IpAddr = IpAddr::V4(Ipv4Addr::new(10, 0, 0, 1));
+        for _ in 0..30 {
+            assert!(limiter.check_and_consume(ip));
+        }
+        // 31st should be rejected.
+        assert!(!limiter.check_and_consume(ip));
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn rate_limiter_prune_clears_stale() {
+        let limiter = RateLimiter::new(5);
+        let ip: IpAddr = IpAddr::V4(Ipv4Addr::new(1, 2, 3, 4));
+        let _ = limiter.check_and_consume(ip);
+        assert_eq!(limiter.buckets.lock().unwrap().len(), 1);
+        // Manually age the entry past the 60s prune threshold.
+        {
+            let mut b = limiter.buckets.lock().unwrap();
+            b.get_mut(&ip).unwrap().last_refill = Instant::now() - Duration::from_secs(61);
+        }
+        limiter.prune();
+        assert_eq!(limiter.buckets.lock().unwrap().len(), 0);
+    }
+}

+//! Gatewarden Bridge — language-agnostic HTTP sidecar for Gatewarden validation.
+//!
+//! Starts an HTTP server (default: 127.0.0.1:4760) that exposes Gatewarden
+//! license validation via a simple JSON API, enabling TypeScript, Python,
+//! Go, and any other language to use hardened Keygen validation without
+//! reimplementing Ed25519 signature verification.
+//!
+//! # Usage
+//!
+//! ```bash
+//! gatewarden-bridge bridge.toml
+//! ```
+//!
+//! # Config format (bridge.toml)
+//!
+//! ```toml
+//! port = 4760
+//! bind = "127.0.0.1"   # loopback-only; never expose to the internet
+//!
+//! [profiles.myapp-pro]
+//! account_id        = "your-keygen-account-uuid"
+//! public_key_hex    = "64-hex-char-ed25519-verify-key-from-keygen-dashboard"
+//! required_entitlements = ["PRO"]
+//! offline_grace_secs    = 86400
+//! ```
+
+mod auth;
+mod config;
+mod routes;
+mod state;
+
+use axum::{
+    middleware,
+    routing::{get, post},
+    Router,
+};
+use clap::Parser;
+use std::net::SocketAddr;
+use std::sync::Arc;
+use tracing_subscriber::EnvFilter;
+
+#[derive(Parser)]
+#[command(
+    name = "gatewarden-bridge",
+    about = "Language-agnostic HTTP bridge for Gatewarden license validation",
+    version
+)]
+struct Cli {
+    /// Path to bridge.toml config file
+    #[arg(default_value = "bridge.toml")]
+    config: String,
+}
+
+#[tokio::main]
+async fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
+    // Initialise structured logging (RUST_LOG=info by default)
+    tracing_subscriber::fmt()
+        .with_env_filter(EnvFilter::from_default_env().add_directive("info".parse()?))
+        .init();
+
+    let cli = Cli::parse();
+
+    tracing::info!("Loading config from '{}'", cli.config);
+    let bridge_config = config::BridgeConfig::load(&cli.config)?;
+    let addr = bridge_config.listen_addr();
+
+    tracing::info!(
+        "Starting Gatewarden Bridge v{} with {} profile(s)",
+        env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"),
+        bridge_config.profiles.len()
+    );
+
+    let state = Arc::new(
+        tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || state::AppState::new(bridge_config))
+            .await
+            .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!("Failed to initialize bridge state: {}", e))??,
+    );
+
+    // Log FSE plan stats for each profile
+    for (profile_name, manager) in &state.managers {
+        let plan = manager.fse_plan();
+        tracing::info!(
+            "Profile '{}': {} rules, {} unique selectors",
+            profile_name,
+            plan.rules.len(),
+            plan.selectors.len()
+        );
+    }
+
+    // Authenticated sub-router — bearer token + rate limit applied here.
+    let authed_token = state.bearer_token.clone();
+    let authed_state = state.clone();
+    let mut authed = Router::new()
+        .route("/v1/health", get(routes::health))
+        .route("/v1/validate-key", post(routes::validate_key))
+        .route("/v1/check-access", post(routes::check_access));
+
+    #[cfg(feature = "meter")]
+    {
+        authed = authed.route("/v1/record-use", post(routes::record_use));
+    }
+
+    let authed = authed
+        .layer(middleware::from_fn(move |headers, req, next| {
+            let token = authed_token.clone();
+            auth::require_bearer_token(headers, token, req, next)
+        }))
+        .layer(middleware::from_fn_with_state(
+            authed_state.clone(),
+            routes::rate_limit_layer,
+        ))
+        .with_state(authed_state);
+
+    let app = Router::new()
+        .merge(authed)
+        // OpenAPI spec is public (no secrets, just schema).
+        .route("/.well-known/openapi.json", get(routes::openapi_spec));
+
+    tracing::info!("Listening on http://{}", addr);
+
+    // Spawn background task to prune stale rate-limiter buckets every 60 seconds.
+    let prune_state = state.clone();
+    tokio::spawn(async move {
+        loop {
+            tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_secs(60)).await;
+            prune_state.rate_limiter.prune();
+        }
+    });
+
+    let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind(&addr)
+        .await
+        .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!("Cannot bind to {}: {}", addr, e))?;
+
+    axum::serve(
+        listener,
+        app.into_make_service_with_connect_info::<SocketAddr>(),
+    )
+    .await?;
+
+    Ok(())
+}

+//! File-based cache backend with atomic writes.
+//!
+//! Stores authenticated cache records under `dirs::data_dir()/<namespace>/`.
+//! Uses temp file + rename for atomic writes.
+
+use crate::cache::format::CacheRecord;
+use crate::GatewardenError;
+use std::fs;
+use std::path::PathBuf;
+
+/// File-based cache backend.
+pub struct FileCache {
+    /// Directory for cache files.
+    cache_dir: PathBuf,
+}
+
+impl FileCache {
+    /// Create a new file cache with the given namespace.
+    ///
+    /// Cache files are stored under `dirs::data_dir()/<namespace>/`.
+    pub fn new(namespace: &str) -> Result<Self, GatewardenError> {
+        let base_dir = dirs::data_dir()
+            .ok_or_else(|| GatewardenError::CacheIO("Could not find data directory".to_string()))?;
+
+        let cache_dir = base_dir.join(namespace);
+
+        // Ensure directory exists
+        fs::create_dir_all(&cache_dir)
+            .map_err(|e| GatewardenError::CacheIO(format!("Failed to create cache dir: {}", e)))?;
+
+        Ok(Self { cache_dir })
+    }
+
+    /// Create a file cache at a specific path (for testing).
+    #[cfg(test)]
+    pub fn with_path(cache_dir: PathBuf) -> Result<Self, GatewardenError> {
+        fs::create_dir_all(&cache_dir)
+            .map_err(|e| GatewardenError::CacheIO(format!("Failed to create cache dir: {}", e)))?;
+        Ok(Self { cache_dir })
+    }
+
+    /// Get the path for a license cache file.
+    fn license_path(&self, license_key_hash: &str) -> PathBuf {
+        // Use first 16 chars of hash as filename to avoid exposing full key
+        let safe_name = &license_key_hash[..16.min(license_key_hash.len())];
+        self.cache_dir.join(format!("{}.json", safe_name))
+    }
+
+    /// Save a cache record atomically.
+    ///
+    /// Uses temp file + rename for atomic write.
+    pub fn save(
+        &self,
+        license_key_hash: &str,
+        record: &CacheRecord,
+    ) -> Result<(), GatewardenError> {
+        let target_path = self.license_path(license_key_hash);
+        // Avoid using the full hash in filenames.
+        let safe_name = &license_key_hash[..16.min(license_key_hash.len())];
+        let temp_path = self.cache_dir.join(format!("{}.tmp", safe_name));
+
+        let json = record.to_json()?;
+
+        // Write to temp file
+        fs::write(&temp_path, &json)
+            .map_err(|e| GatewardenError::CacheIO(format!("Failed to write temp file: {}", e)))?;
+
+        // Best-effort restrict permissions on Unix-like systems.
+        #[cfg(unix)]
+        {
+            use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;
+            let perms = fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o600);
+            let _ = fs::set_permissions(&temp_path, perms);
+        }
+
+        // Atomic rename on Unix; on Windows rename-over-existing fails.
+        if target_path.exists() {
+            fs::remove_file(&target_path).map_err(|e| {
+                GatewardenError::CacheIO(format!("Failed to remove old cache file: {}", e))
+            })?;
+        }
+        fs::rename(&temp_path, &target_path)
+            .map_err(|e| GatewardenError::CacheIO(format!("Failed to rename cache file: {}", e)))?;
+
+        Ok(())
+    }
+
+    /// Load a cache record.
+    pub fn load(&self, license_key_hash: &str) -> Result<Option<CacheRecord>, GatewardenError> {
+        let path = self.license_path(license_key_hash);
+
+        if !path.exists() {
+            return Ok(None);
+        }
+
+        let json = fs::read_to_string(&path)
+            .map_err(|e| GatewardenError::CacheIO(format!("Failed to read cache file: {}", e)))?;
+
+        let record = CacheRecord::from_json(&json)?;
+        Ok(Some(record))
+    }
+
+    /// Delete a cache record.
+    pub fn delete(&self, license_key_hash: &str) -> Result<(), GatewardenError> {
+        let path = self.license_path(license_key_hash);
+
+        if path.exists() {
+            fs::remove_file(&path)
+                .map_err(|e| GatewardenError::CacheIO(format!("Failed to delete cache: {}", e)))?;
+        }
+
+        Ok(())
+    }
+
+    /// Clear all cache files.
+    pub fn clear(&self) -> Result<(), GatewardenError> {
+        for entry in fs::read_dir(&self.cache_dir)
+            .map_err(|e| GatewardenError::CacheIO(format!("Failed to read cache dir: {}", e)))?
+        {
+            let entry = entry
+                .map_err(|e| GatewardenError::CacheIO(format!("Failed to read entry: {}", e)))?;
+            let path = entry.path();
+            if path.extension().is_some_and(|ext| ext == "json") {
+                fs::remove_file(&path)
+                    .map_err(|e| GatewardenError::CacheIO(format!("Failed to delete: {}", e)))?;
+            }
+        }
+        Ok(())
+    }
+}
+
+/// Compute a SHA-256 hash of the license key for use as cache key.
+///
+/// This avoids storing the raw license key in filenames.
+pub fn hash_license_key(license_key: &str) -> String {
+    use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};
+    let hash = Sha256::digest(license_key.as_bytes());
+    hex::encode(hash)
+}
+
+#[cfg(test)]
+mod tests {
+    use super::*;
+    use crate::cache::format::CacheRecord;
+    use crate::clock::MockClock;
+    use chrono::{TimeZone, Utc};
+    use tempfile::TempDir;
+
+    fn make_test_record(clock: &MockClock) -> CacheRecord {
+        CacheRecord::new(
+            "Wed, 15 Jan 2025 12:00:00 GMT".to_string(),
+            r#"algorithm="ed25519", signature="test""#.to_string(),
+            Some("sha-256=abc123".to_string()),
+            r#"{"data":{"valid":true}}"#.to_string(),
+            "/v1/accounts/test/licenses/abc/actions/validate".to_string(),
+            "api.keygen.sh".to_string(),
+            clock,
+        )
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn test_file_cache_roundtrip() {
+        let temp_dir = TempDir::new().unwrap();
+        let cache = FileCache::with_path(temp_dir.path().to_path_buf()).unwrap();
+
+        let clock = MockClock::new(Utc.with_ymd_and_hms(2025, 1, 15, 12, 0, 0).unwrap());
+        let record = make_test_record(&clock);
+        let key_hash = hash_license_key("test-license-key");
+
+        // Save
+        cache.save(&key_hash, &record).unwrap();
+
+        // Load
+        let loaded = cache.load(&key_hash).unwrap();
+        assert!(loaded.is_some());
+        let loaded = loaded.unwrap();
+        assert_eq!(loaded.body, record.body);
+        assert_eq!(loaded.date, record.date);
+        assert_eq!(loaded.signature, record.signature);
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn test_file_cache_load_nonexistent() {
+        let temp_dir = TempDir::new().unwrap();
+        let cache = FileCache::with_path(temp_dir.path().to_path_buf()).unwrap();
+
+        let key_hash = hash_license_key("nonexistent");
+        let loaded = cache.load(&key_hash).unwrap();
+        assert!(loaded.is_none());
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn test_file_cache_delete() {
+        let temp_dir = TempDir::new().unwrap();
+        let cache = FileCache::with_path(temp_dir.path().to_path_buf()).unwrap();
+
+        let clock = MockClock::new(Utc.with_ymd_and_hms(2025, 1, 15, 12, 0, 0).unwrap());
+        let record = make_test_record(&clock);
+        let key_hash = hash_license_key("test-license-key");
+
+        cache.save(&key_hash, &record).unwrap();
+        assert!(cache.load(&key_hash).unwrap().is_some());
+
+        cache.delete(&key_hash).unwrap();
+        assert!(cache.load(&key_hash).unwrap().is_none());
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn test_file_cache_clear() {
+        let temp_dir = TempDir::new().unwrap();
+        let cache = FileCache::with_path(temp_dir.path().to_path_buf()).unwrap();
+
+        let clock = MockClock::new(Utc.with_ymd_and_hms(2025, 1, 15, 12, 0, 0).unwrap());
+        let record = make_test_record(&clock);
+
+        cache.save(&hash_license_key("key1"), &record).unwrap();
+        cache.save(&hash_license_key("key2"), &record).unwrap();
+
+        cache.clear().unwrap();
+
+        assert!(cache.load(&hash_license_key("key1")).unwrap().is_none());
+        assert!(cache.load(&hash_license_key("key2")).unwrap().is_none());
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn test_hash_license_key() {
+        let hash1 = hash_license_key("test-key-1");
+        let hash2 = hash_license_key("test-key-1");
+        let hash3 = hash_license_key("test-key-2");
+
+        // Same input produces same output
+        assert_eq!(hash1, hash2);
+        // Different input produces different output
+        assert_ne!(hash1, hash3);
+        // Output is 64 hex chars (256 bits)
+        assert_eq!(hash1.len(), 64);
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn test_file_cache_atomic_write() {
+        let temp_dir = TempDir::new().unwrap();
+        let cache = FileCache::with_path(temp_dir.path().to_path_buf()).unwrap();
+
+        let clock = MockClock::new(Utc.with_ymd_and_hms(2025, 1, 15, 12, 0, 0).unwrap());
+        let record1 = make_test_record(&clock);
+        let key_hash = hash_license_key("test-key");
+
+        // Save first record
+        cache.save(&key_hash, &record1).unwrap();
+
+        // Create updated record
+        let mut record2 = make_test_record(&clock);
+        record2.body = r#"{"data":{"valid":false}}"#.to_string();
+
+        // Save updated record (atomic, should not corrupt if interrupted)
+        cache.save(&key_hash, &record2).unwrap();
+
+        // Load should give us the updated record
+        let loaded = cache.load(&key_hash).unwrap().unwrap();
+        assert_eq!(loaded.body, record2.body);
+    }
+}

-//! Authenticated cache record format.
-//!
-//! The cache record stores all data needed to re-verify a Keygen response:
-//! - Original response body
-//! - HTTP headers needed for signature verification (Date, Keygen-Signature, Digest)
-//! - Timestamp when the record was cached
-//!
-//! On load, we:
-//! 1. Re-verify the signature (required)
-//! 2. Compare digest if present
-//! 3. Check `now - cached_at <= offline_grace`
-
-use crate::clock::Clock;
-use crate::crypto::{
-    digest::verify_digest,
-    signing::build_signing_string,
-    verify::{decode_public_key, parse_signature_header, verify_ed25519},
-};
-use crate::GatewardenError;
-use chrono::{DateTime, Utc};
-use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
-use std::time::Duration;
-
-/// Authenticated cache record containing all data needed to re-verify.
-#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
-pub struct CacheRecord {
-    /// The original HTTP Date header value.
-    pub date: String,
-
-    /// The original Keygen-Signature header value.
-    pub signature: String,
-
-    /// The original Digest header value (optional).
-    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
-    pub digest: Option<String>,
-
-    /// The original response body (JSON).
-    pub body: String,
-
-    /// When this record was cached (ISO 8601).
-    pub cached_at: DateTime<Utc>,
-
-    /// Request path used for signing string reconstruction.
-    /// E.g., "/v1/accounts/{account}/licenses/{id}/actions/validate"
-    pub request_path: String,
-
-    /// Host used for signing string reconstruction.
-    pub host: String,
-}
-
-impl CacheRecord {
-    /// Create a new cache record from response data.
-    pub fn new(
-        date: String,
-        signature: String,
-        digest: Option<String>,
-        body: String,
-        request_path: String,
-        host: String,
-        clock: &dyn Clock,
-    ) -> Self {
-        Self {
-            date,
-            signature,
-            digest,
-            body,
-            cached_at: clock.now_utc(),
-            request_path,
-            host,
-        }
-    }
-
-    /// Serialize the cache record to JSON.
-    pub fn to_json(&self) -> Result<String, GatewardenError> {
-        serde_json::to_string_pretty(self)
-            .map_err(|e| GatewardenError::CacheIO(format!("Failed to serialize cache: {}", e)))
-    }
-
-    /// Deserialize a cache record from JSON.
-    pub fn from_json(json: &str) -> Result<Self, GatewardenError> {
-        serde_json::from_str(json)
-            .map_err(|e| GatewardenError::CacheIO(format!("Failed to deserialize cache: {}", e)))
-    }
-
-    /// Verify the cached record is authentic and within offline grace.
-    ///
-    /// This performs:
-    /// 1. Signature verification (required)
-    /// 2. Digest comparison (if present)
-    /// 3. Offline grace check
-    ///
-    /// Note: We do NOT apply the 5-minute replay window to cached records.
-    /// The `offline_grace` parameter controls how long cached data is valid.
-    pub fn verify(
-        &self,
-        public_key_hex: &str,
-        offline_grace: Duration,
-        clock: &dyn Clock,
-    ) -> Result<(), GatewardenError> {
-        // 1. Parse signature header
-        let parsed_sig = parse_signature_header(&self.signature)?;
-
-        // 2. Decode public key
-        let verifying_key = decode_public_key(public_key_hex)?;
-
-        // 3. Reconstruct signing string
-        // For POST validate requests, Keygen signs: (request-target), host, date, digest
-        let signing_string = build_signing_string(
-            "post",
-            &self.request_path,
-            &self.host,
-            &self.date,
-            self.digest.as_deref(),
-        );
-
-        // 4. Verify Ed25519 signature
-        verify_ed25519(&parsed_sig.signature, &signing_string, &verifying_key)
-            .map_err(|_| GatewardenError::CacheTampered)?;
-
-        // 5. Verify digest if present
-        if let Some(ref digest_header) = self.digest {
-            verify_digest(self.body.as_bytes(), Some(digest_header))
-                .map_err(|_| GatewardenError::CacheTampered)?;
-        }
-
-        // 6. Check offline grace period
-        let now = clock.now_utc();
-        let age = now.signed_duration_since(self.cached_at);
-        let grace_secs = offline_grace.as_secs() as i64;
-
-        if age.num_seconds() > grace_secs {
-            return Err(GatewardenError::CacheExpired);
-        }
-
-        // Also reject if cached_at is in the future (clock tampering)
-        if age.num_seconds() < 0 {
-            return Err(GatewardenError::CacheTampered);
-        }
-
-        Ok(())
-    }
-
-    /// Extract the cached response body.
-    pub fn body(&self) -> &str {
-        &self.body
-    }
-}
-
-#[cfg(test)]
-mod tests {

+//! Authenticated cache record format.
+//!
+//! The cache record stores all data needed to re-verify a Keygen response:
+//! - Original response body
+//! - HTTP headers needed for signature verification (Date, Keygen-Signature, Digest)
+//! - Timestamp when the record was cached
+//!
+//! On load, we:
+//! 1. Re-verify the signature (required)
+//! 2. Compare digest if present
+//! 3. Check `now - cached_at <= offline_grace`
+
+use crate::clock::Clock;
+use crate::crypto::{
+    digest::verify_digest,
+    signing::build_signing_string,
+    verify::{decode_public_key, parse_signature_header, verify_ed25519},
+};
+use crate::GatewardenError;
+use chrono::{DateTime, Utc};
+use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
+use std::time::Duration;
+
+/// Authenticated cache record containing all data needed to re-verify.
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
+pub struct CacheRecord {
+    /// The original HTTP Date header value.
+    pub date: String,
+
+    /// The original Keygen-Signature header value.
+    pub signature: String,
+
+    /// The original Digest header value (optional).
+    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
+    pub digest: Option<String>,
+
+    /// The original response body (JSON).
+    pub body: String,
+
+    /// When this record was cached (ISO 8601).
+    pub cached_at: DateTime<Utc>,
+
+    /// Request path used for signing string reconstruction.
+    /// E.g., "/v1/accounts/{account}/licenses/{id}/actions/validate"
+    pub request_path: String,
+
+    /// Host used for signing string reconstruction.
+    pub host: String,
+}
+
+impl CacheRecord {
+    /// Create a new cache record from response data.
+    pub fn new(
+        date: String,
+        signature: String,
+        digest: Option<String>,
+        body: String,
+        request_path: String,
+        host: String,
+        clock: &dyn Clock,
+    ) -> Self {
+        Self {
+            date,
+            signature,
+            digest,
+            body,
+            cached_at: clock.now_utc(),
+            request_path,
+            host,
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// Serialize the cache record to JSON.
+    pub fn to_json(&self) -> Result<String, GatewardenError> {
+        serde_json::to_string_pretty(self)
+            .map_err(|e| GatewardenError::CacheIO(format!("Failed to serialize cache: {}", e)))
+    }
+
+    /// Deserialize a cache record from JSON.
+    pub fn from_json(json: &str) -> Result<Self, GatewardenError> {
+        serde_json::from_str(json)
+            .map_err(|e| GatewardenError::CacheIO(format!("Failed to deserialize cache: {}", e)))
+    }
+
+    /// Verify the cached record is authentic and within offline grace.
+    ///
+    /// This performs:
+    /// 1. Signature verification (required)
+    /// 2. Digest comparison (if present)
+    /// 3. Offline grace check
+    ///
+    /// Note: We do NOT apply the 5-minute replay window to cached records.
+    /// The `offline_grace` parameter controls how long cached data is valid.
+    pub fn verify(
+        &self,
+        public_key_hex: &str,
+        offline_grace: Duration,
+        clock: &dyn Clock,
+    ) -> Result<(), GatewardenError> {
+        // 1. Parse signature header
+        let parsed_sig = parse_signature_header(&self.signature)?;
+
+        // 2. Decode public key
+        let verifying_key = decode_public_key(public_key_hex)?;
+
+        // 3. Reconstruct signing string
+        // For POST validate requests, Keygen signs: (request-target), host, date, digest
+        let signing_string = build_signing_string(
+            "post",
+            &self.request_path,
+            &self.host,
+            &self.date,
+            self.digest.as_deref(),
+        );
+
+        // 4. Verify Ed25519 signature
+        verify_ed25519(&parsed_sig.signature, &signing_string, &verifying_key)
+            .map_err(|_| GatewardenError::CacheTampered)?;
+
+        // 5. Verify digest if present
+        if let Some(ref digest_header) = self.digest {
+            verify_digest(self.body.as_bytes(), Some(digest_header))
+                .map_err(|_| GatewardenError::CacheTampered)?;
+        }
+
+        // 6. Check offline grace period
+        let now = clock.now_utc();
+        let age = now.signed_duration_since(self.cached_at);
+        let grace_secs = offline_grace.as_secs() as i64;
+
+        if age.num_seconds() > grace_secs {
+            return Err(GatewardenError::CacheExpired);
+        }
+
+        // Also reject if cached_at is in the future (clock tampering)
+        if age.num_seconds() < 0 {
+            return Err(GatewardenError::CacheTampered);
+        }
+
+        Ok(())
+    }
+
+    /// Extract the cached response body.
+    pub fn body(&self) -> &str {
+        &self.body
+    }
+}
+
+#[cfg(test)]
+mod tests {
+    use super::*;
+    use crate::clock::MockClock;
+    use crate::crypto::digest::format_digest_header;
+    use base64::{engine::general_purpose::STANDARD, Engine};
+    use chrono::TimeZone;
+    use ed25519_dalek::{Signer, SigningKey};
+
+    // Test signing seed + verifying key (DO NOT USE IN PRODUCTION)
+    // This is a well-known Ed25519 test vector seed.
+    const TEST_SIGNING_SEED_BYTES: [u8; 32] = [
+        0x9d, 0x61, 0xb1, 0x9d, 0xef, 0xfd, 0x5a, 0x60, 0xba, 0x84, 0x4a, 0xf4, 0x92, 0xec, 0x2c,
+        0xc4, 0x44, 0x49, 0xc5, 0x69, 0x7b, 0x32, 0x69, 0x19, 0x70, 0x3b, 0xac, 0x03, 0x1c, 0xae,
+        0x7f, 0x60,
+    ];
+    const TEST_VERIFY_KEY_HEX: &str =
+        "d75a980182b10ab7d54bfed3c964073a0ee172f3daa62325af021a68f707511a";
+
+    fn get_test_signing_key() -> SigningKey {
+        SigningKey::from_bytes(&TEST_SIGNING_SEED_BYTES)
+    }
+
+    fn sign_test_data(signing_string: &str) -> String {
+        let signing_key = get_test_signing_key();
+        let signature = signing_key.sign(signing_string.as_bytes());
+        STANDARD.encode(signature.to_bytes())
+    }
+
+    fn create_test_record(
+        body: &str,
+        date: &str,
+        host: &str,
+        path: &str,
+        clock: &MockClock,
+    ) -> CacheRecord {
+        let digest = format_digest_header(body.as_bytes());
+        let signing_string = build_signing_string("post", path, host, date, Some(&digest));
+        let signature_b64 = sign_test_data(&signing_string);
+        let signature_header = format!(r#"algorithm="ed25519", signature="{}""#, signature_b64);
+
+        CacheRecord::new(
+            date.to_string(),
+            signature_header,
+            Some(digest),
+            body.to_string(),
+            path.to_string(),
+            host.to_string(),
+            clock,
+        )
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn test_cache_record_roundtrip() {
+        let clock = MockClock::new(Utc.with_ymd_and_hms(2025, 1, 15, 12, 0, 0).unwrap());
+        let body = r#"{"data":{"type":"licenses","attributes":{"valid":true}}}"#;
+        let record = create_test_record(
+            body,
+            "Wed, 15 Jan 2025 12:00:00 GMT",
+            "api.keygen.sh",
+            "/v1/accounts/test/licenses/abc/actions/validate",
+            &clock,
+        );
+
+        let json = record.to_json().unwrap();
+        let restored = CacheRecord::from_json(&json).unwrap();
+
+        assert_eq!(restored.body, body);
+        assert_eq!(restored.date, record.date);
+        assert_eq!(restored.signature, record.signature);
+        assert_eq!(restored.digest, record.digest);
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn test_cache_record_verify_valid() {
+        let clock = MockClock::new(Utc.with_ymd_and_hms(2025, 1, 15, 12, 0, 0).unwrap());
+        let body = r#"{"data":{"type":"licenses","attributes":{"valid":true}}}"#;
+        let record = create_test_record(
+            body,
+            "Wed, 15 Jan 2025 12:00:00 GMT",
+            "api.keygen.sh",
+            "/v1/accounts/test/licenses/abc/actions/validate",
+            &clock,
+        );
+
+        // Verify immediately - should pass
+        let result = record.verify(
+            TEST_VERIFY_KEY_HEX,
+            Duration::from_secs(86400), // 24 hours grace
+            &clock,
+        );
+        assert!(result.is_ok());
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn test_cache_record_verify_within_grace() {
+        let clock = MockClock::new(Utc.with_ymd_and_hms(2025, 1, 15, 12, 0, 0).unwrap());
+        let body = r#"{"data":{"type":"licenses","attributes":{"valid":true}}}"#;
+        let record = create_test_record(
+            body,
+            "Wed, 15 Jan 2025 12:00:00 GMT",
+            "api.keygen.sh",
+            "/v1/accounts/test/licenses/abc/actions/validate",
+            &clock,
+        );
+
+        // Advance 23 hours (within 24-hour grace)
+        let later_clock = MockClock::new(Utc.with_ymd_and_hms(2025, 1, 16, 11, 0, 0).unwrap());
+        let result = record.verify(
+            TEST_VERIFY_KEY_HEX,
+            Duration::from_secs(86400), // 24 hours grace
+            &later_clock,
+        );
+        assert!(result.is_ok());
+    }
+

+        let body = r#"{"data":{"type":"licenses","attributes":{"valid":true}}}"#;

+        let body = r#"{"data":{"type":"licenses","attributes":{"valid":true}}}"#;
+        let mut record = create_test_record(
+            body,
+            "Wed, 15 Jan 2025 12:00:00 GMT",
+            "api.keygen.sh",
+            "/v1/accounts/test/licenses/abc/actions/validate",
+            &clock,
+        );
+
+        // Tamper with signature by using a completely different base64 value
+        record.signature = r#"algorithm="ed25519", signature="AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA==""#.to_string();
+
+        let result = record.verify(TEST_VERIFY_KEY_HEX, Duration::from_secs(86400), &clock);
+        assert!(matches!(result, Err(GatewardenError::CacheTampered)));
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn test_cache_record_future_cached_at() {
+        let clock = MockClock::new(Utc.with_ymd_and_hms(2025, 1, 15, 12, 0, 0).unwrap());
+        let body = r#"{"data":{"type":"licenses","attributes":{"valid":true}}}"#;
+        let record = create_test_record(
+            body,
+            "Wed, 15 Jan 2025 12:00:00 GMT",
+            "api.keygen.sh",
+            "/v1/accounts/test/licenses/abc/actions/validate",
+            &clock,
+        );
+
+        // Verify with a clock that's BEFORE the cached_at time
+        let past_clock = MockClock::new(Utc.with_ymd_and_hms(2025, 1, 15, 11, 0, 0).unwrap());
+        let result = record.verify(TEST_VERIFY_KEY_HEX, Duration::from_secs(86400), &past_clock);
+        assert!(matches!(result, Err(GatewardenError::CacheTampered)));
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn test_cache_record_no_digest() {
+        let clock = MockClock::new(Utc.with_ymd_and_hms(2025, 1, 15, 12, 0, 0).unwrap());
+        let body = r#"{"data":{"type":"licenses","attributes":{"valid":true}}}"#;
+        let date = "Wed, 15 Jan 2025 12:00:00 GMT";
+        let host = "api.keygen.sh";
+        let path = "/v1/accounts/test/licenses/abc/actions/validate";
+
+        // Sign without digest
+        let signing_string = build_signing_string("post", path, host, date, None);
+        let signature_b64 = sign_test_data(&signing_string);
+        let signature_header = format!(r#"algorithm="ed25519", signature="{}""#, signature_b64);
+
+        let record = CacheRecord::new(
+            date.to_string(),
+            signature_header,
+            None, // No digest
+            body.to_string(),
+            path.to_string(),
+            host.to_string(),
+            &clock,
+        );
+
+        let result = record.verify(TEST_VERIFY_KEY_HEX, Duration::from_secs(86400), &clock);
+        assert!(result.is_ok());
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn test_cache_record_grace_boundary() {
+        let clock = MockClock::new(Utc.with_ymd_and_hms(2025, 1, 15, 12, 0, 0).unwrap());
+        let body = r#"{"data":{"type":"licenses","attributes":{"valid":true}}}"#;
+        let record = create_test_record(
+            body,
+            "Wed, 15 Jan 2025 12:00:00 GMT",
+            "api.keygen.sh",
+            "/v1/accounts/test/licenses/abc/actions/validate",
+            &clock,
+        );
+
+        // Exactly at grace boundary (should pass)
+        let boundary_clock = MockClock::new(Utc.with_ymd_and_hms(2025, 1, 16, 12, 0, 0).unwrap());
+        let result = record.verify(
+            TEST_VERIFY_KEY_HEX,
+            Duration::from_secs(86400), // 24 hours
+            &boundary_clock,
+        );
+        assert!(result.is_ok());
+
+        // One second over (should fail)
+        let over_clock = MockClock::new(Utc.with_ymd_and_hms(2025, 1, 16, 12, 0, 1).unwrap());
+        let result = record.verify(TEST_VERIFY_KEY_HEX, Duration::from_secs(86400), &over_clock);
+        assert!(matches!(result, Err(GatewardenError::CacheExpired)));
+    }
+}

+//! Gatewarden configuration.
+
+use std::time::Duration;
+
+use crate::policy::fse::model::Rule as FseRule;
+
+/// Configuration for Gatewarden license validation.
+///
+/// This struct contains all product-specific settings needed to validate
+/// licenses against Keygen.sh.
+///
+/// # Security note
+/// `account_id` and `public_key_hex` should be embedded in your application at
+/// compile time where possible, not loaded from untrusted environment variables.
+/// The types are `String` so the bridge and serverless deployments can load them
+/// from a secrets store at startup.
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
+pub struct GatewardenConfig {
+    /// Application name (e.g., "shimmy", "crabcamera")
+    pub app_name: String,
+
+    /// Feature name (e.g., "vision", "pro")
+    pub feature_name: String,
+
+    /// Keygen account ID (UUID format).
+    /// Embed in your binary; do not load from untrusted user input.
+    pub account_id: String,
+
+    /// Keygen Ed25519 public key (hex-encoded, 64 characters).
+    /// Embed in your binary; do not load from untrusted user input.
+    pub public_key_hex: String,
+
+    /// Required entitlement codes that the license must have.
+    /// All codes must be present for access to be granted.
+    pub required_entitlements: Vec<String>,
+
+    /// User-Agent product identifier (e.g., "shimmy-vision").
+    /// Used by Keygen for crack detection analytics.
+    pub user_agent_product: String,
+
+    /// Cache namespace for storing license data.
+    /// Each product should use a unique namespace to avoid collisions.
+    pub cache_namespace: String,
+
+    /// Grace period for offline operation.
+    /// Cached licenses remain valid for this duration after last successful online validation.
+    pub offline_grace: Duration,
+
+    /// Additional custom FSE rules merged into the default plan.
+    ///
+    /// Lets callers express policy beyond the built-in signature/state/
+    /// entitlement checks — e.g. `maxUses`-style usage caps via the
+    /// `UsageRemaining` selector. Combined with `compile_default_plan`.
+    pub custom_rules: Vec<FseRule>,
+}
+
+impl GatewardenConfig {
+    /// Validate configuration for obvious errors.
+    pub fn validate(&self) -> Result<(), crate::GatewardenError> {
+        if self.account_id.is_empty() {
+            return Err(crate::GatewardenError::ConfigError(
+                "account_id cannot be empty".to_string(),
+            ));
+        }
+        if self.public_key_hex.len() != 64 {
+            return Err(crate::GatewardenError::ConfigError(format!(
+                "public_key_hex must be 64 hex characters, got {}",
+                self.public_key_hex.len()
+            )));
+        }
+        if self.cache_namespace.is_empty() {
+            return Err(crate::GatewardenError::ConfigError(
+                "cache_namespace cannot be empty".to_string(),
+            ));
+        }
+        Ok(())
+    }
+}
